screening_decisions.reason: Randomized controlled trial but uses intravenous clomipramine, not orally administered as required.
Randomized controlled trial but evaluates fluoxetine (an SSRI), not a tricyclic drug.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of oral nortriptyline (tricyclic antidepressant) in depressed adolescents aged 12-17 years.
Literature review, not a randomized controlled trial.

Double-blind pilot study of oral imipramine (tricyclic) vs placebo in depressed children. Use of child-specific depression scales (BID, SADLI, CDI) indicates pediatric sample likely within 6-18 years age range.
Double-blind crossover pilot study of oral amitriptyline (tricyclic) vs placebo in children with MDD aged 9-12 years.
Focuses on newer generation antidepressants (SSRIs), not tricyclic drugs; appears to be a review/protocol, not an RCT reporting tricyclic vs placebo comparison.

Randomized, double-blind trial comparing imipramine (tricyclic) + CBT vs placebo + CBT in adolescents with school refusal and comorbid anxiety/depression. CBT is constant across groups, so this tests the efficacy of adding imipramine to CBT.
Five-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of oral imipramine (tricyclic) vs placebo in prepubertal children with major depressive disorder (age range implied as 6-12 years).
Randomized controlled trial with three arms: paroxetine, imipramine (tricyclic), and placebo. Reports imipramine vs placebo comparison for adolescents with major depression.
Review article discussing antidepressant mechanisms, not a randomized controlled trial.
Focuses on overdose safety profiles of SSRIs vs TCAs, not an efficacy RCT comparing tricyclic drug to placebo.
Discusses statistical methods for meta-analysis, not an RCT of tricyclic antidepressants.
Studies clinical findings in amitriptyline poisoning/intoxication, not an efficacy RCT of antidepressant treatment.
Secondary analysis predicting treatment response based on concomitant disorders; does not specify the drug is tricyclic and is not a primary RCT report.
Randomized controlled trial of oral desipramine (tricyclic) vs placebo in adolescents (ages 13-18) with major depression.
Review article describing current status and future directions, not a randomized controlled trial.
Includes a double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing imipramine (tricyclic) to placebo (along with alprazolam) in adolescents with school refusal and comorbid anxiety/depression.
Studies accidental ingestions/poisoning of tricyclic antidepressants, not an efficacy RCT.
Randomized, controlled trial of oral amitriptyline (tricyclic) vs placebo in adolescents aged 12-17 years with major depressive disorder.

Double-blind trial of oral clomipramine (tricyclic) vs placebo (both with psychotherapy) in children with school refusal and neurotic disorder (which includes depression). School phobia context suggests school-aged children within 6-18 years.
Meta-analysis of studies involving patients aged 18-65 years (outside 6-18 range); compares paroxetine to amitriptyline but is not a primary RCT.
Studies imipramine treatment and plasma level correlations but lacks a placebo control group; compares high vs low plasma levels, not drug vs placebo.
Randomized, controlled trial of oral amitriptyline (tricyclic) vs placebo in adolescents with treatment-resistant major depressive disorder.

Eight-week double-blind study of imipramine (tricyclic) vs placebo, both combined with cognitive-behavioral therapy for school refusal, in anxious-depressed adolescents. Tests compliance but includes the efficacy comparison.
